deep.reconstruction:
The page holds two reductions of single solar altitudes taken with a sextant and artificial horizon. Each reduction gives local true time and the clock correction. The working latitude is 52°16'5", which suggests Braunschweig, so the page probably dates from Gauss's years there (before 1807); the place is inferred, not stated.

A. MORNING SET (top left).
1. Double altitudes 2h' = 39°30'0" and 40°30'0".
2. Index correction −13'15", then halve: h' = 19°38'22.5" and 20°8'22.5".
3. Subtract refraction minus parallax (2'38.6", 2'34.3"): 19°35'43.9" and 20°5'48.2".
4. Add the solar semidiameter 16'16.7" to get the altitude of the Sun's centre: h1 = 19°52'1", h7 = 20°22'5". The middle value 20°7'3" is their mean.
5. With latitude φ = 52°16'5" and polar distance p = 90° − δ = 101°18'53", 55", 57" (δ ≈ −11°19'):
   - s = (h + φ + p)/2, giving 173°26'59"/2 = 86°43'29.5", and likewise for the other two.
   - s − h = 66°51'28.5", 66°43'58.5", 66°36'28.5".
6. Hour-angle formula: sin²(t/2) = cos s · sin(s−h) / (cos φ · sin p).
7. The 7-place logarithms are, in order:
   - log cos s = 8.7568706, 8.7399118, 8.7222615;
   - log sec φ + log cosec p = 0.2227951, 0.2227960, 0.2227968;
   - log sin(s−h) = 9.9635673, 9.9631611, 9.9627525;
   - their sum 8.9432330, … and its half 9.4716165, ….
8. Because these are morning observations, Gauss reads the half-sum directly as log cos(T/2), where T = 180° − t is the angle counted from midnight. This gives T/2 = 72°46'9.1", 73°7'14.1", 73°28'40.6" and T = 145°32'18.2", 146°14'28.2", 146°57'21.2".
9. Divided by 15, these are true times 9h42m9.2s, 9h44m57.9s, 9h47m49.4s. Four intermediate times (43m5.1s, 45m54.8s, 46m52.0s, and 44m1.3s) are interpolated, giving seven observation times in all.
10. Clock minus true time for the seven observations: +9'34.8", 33.9, 34.2, 33.1, 35.2, 35.3, 34.1. The mean is +9'34.4", noted as 'vor wahrer Zeit voraus' (ahead of true time).
11. Adding the equation of time 15'30.2" gives 25'4.6" 'vor mittlerer Zeit voraus' (ahead of mean time). This sign means the Sun is fast; together with δ ≈ −11.3° it points to late October.
12. A 5-place check of the middle observation: 0.22280 + 8.73982 + 9.96316 = 8.92578, half 9.46289, giving 73°7'20", then 146°14'40", then 9h44m58s.

B. AUXILIARY WORK (top right and centre).
- 2142712 is −log cos φ = 0.2142712. 9914761 and 9913680 are log sin p = 9.9914761 and 9.9913680 for the two polar distances.
- Hence 0.2142712 + 0.0085239 = 0.2227951 (exact) and 0.2142712 + 0.0086320 = 0.2229032 (≈ 0.2229029).
- 21'9"/12 = 1'45.75" is a piece of declination interpolation.
- Daily change of declination 21'8" = 1268". For the interval 4h50m between the morning and afternoon sets: 1268 × 4.833/24 ≈ 255" = 4'15". This matches 101°23'8" − 101°18'53" exactly.
- 2h31m54s + 11m18s = 2.720 h and 2h36m59s + 11m18s = 2.805 h are decimal hours for that interpolation.

C. AFTERNOON SET (bottom).
1. Double altitudes 36°40', 35°40'; index −13'12.5"; halve: 18°13'23.7", 17°43'23.7".
2. Refraction 2'52.8", 2'58.0": 18°10'30.9", 17°40'25.7".
3. Add 16'16.8": 18°26'48" and 17°56'42", with the mean 18°11'45".
4. p = 101°23'8", 10", 12". Then s = 86°3'0.5", 85°55'30", 85°47'59.5" and s − h = 67°36'12.5", 67°43'45", 67°51'17.5".
5. Logs: 8.8381151 + 0.2229029 + 9.9659394 = 9.0269574, half 9.5134787 = log sin(t/2), so t/2 = 19°2'17".
6. Hence t = 38°4'34", 38°42'56", 39°20'48", i.e. 2h32m18.3s, 2h34m51.7s, 2h37m23.2s (with interpolated intermediates).
7. Clock corrections: 9'10.2", 9.9, 9.7, 8.3, 10.1, 9.6, 10.3, mean ≈ 9'9.7" (the mean is not written).

The marginal French 'De huit en huit jours / Depuis' (every eight days / since) is unrelated jotting.
errors: Systematic log slip: Gauss uses −log cos φ = 0.2142712 for φ = 52°16'5". The correct value is 0.2132730 (log cos 52°16'5" = 9.786727, not 9.785729), an error of almost exactly 0.001. It sits in the constants 0.2227951… and 0.2229029…, so every 7-place result on the page inherits it.

Consequence of the slip (my estimate): the morning times come out about 9.8 s too early, so the morning clock correction 9'34.4" should be about 9'24.6". The afternoon times come out about 10.9 s too late, so 9'9.7" should be about 9'20.6". The puzzling 24.7 s disagreement between morning and afternoon on the same day thus shrinks to about 4 s. The page does not show that Gauss noticed this.

The 5-place check writes log cos(86°51'1.5") = 8.73982, but the 7-place value is 8.7399118, so the last digits are off by about 9 units. This makes the check give 73°7'20" instead of 73°7'14" (time 9h44m58.7s vs 9h44m57.9s). Its constant 0.22280 carries the same 0.001 slip.
The sum 0.2142712 + (10 − 9.9913680) gives 0.2229032, while the page has 0.2229029; this is a 3-unit discrepancy in the 7th place.
The semidiameter 16'16.7" is somewhat large for late October (about 16'6"). This may reflect the tables used; it is not a computational error.
All other additions, halvings, arc-to-time conversions and the mean +9'34.4" check correctly.

results.what: Hour angle of the Sun from a measured altitude, latitude and declination, via the half-angle formula sin²(t/2) = cos s sin(s−h)/(cos φ cos δ), with s = (h+φ+p)/2, worked in 7-place logarithms
results.modern_name: Time (clock-correction) determination from single altitudes of the Sun; spherical half-angle formula for the astronomical triangle

results.what: Reduction of sextant/artificial-horizon double altitudes: index error, halving, refraction minus parallax, semidiameter; interpolation of intermediate observation times; mean clock correction; conversion true to mean time by the equation of time
Interpolation of solar declination for an interval of 4h50m from a daily change of 21'8"

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine practical-astronomy computation (a clock correction from solar altitudes) of the kind Gauss did constantly from his Braunschweig years on. The only point of interest is an uncorrected 0.001 slip in log sec φ, which explains most of the morning/afternoon disagreement.
transcription_corrections: '13 15' and '13.12,5' are index corrections of 13'15" and 13'12.5", subtracted before halving.
'72.46.9,1' is written over a struck figure ('7246'); the value is 72°46'9.1".
'2,4' near the top right may be '2^h4' (hours); uncertain.
'-1"4' beside the morning time list is a marginal correction or note of uncertain role.
